title: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight
hook: a teacher walks onto the field just as his two best students raise their maces at each other
carry: a hand on his own thigh

segments.voice: Yesterday: Yudhishthira refused the earth offered from the lake and made a risky offer of his own, and the hidden king came up out of the water to take it. Your line was it isn't yours to give.

Two men face each other on open ground, each holding a heavy iron mace. One is Bhima, of the Pandava brothers. The other is Duryodhana, the Kaurava king, wet from the lake he hid in. Just then a third man arrives, fresh from a long pilgrimage along the holy river Sarasvati. It's Balarama, Krishna's elder brother. He taught both of these men how to fight with the mace. He has stayed out of the whole war. Now he's back in time to watch his two students try to kill each other.
screen: `TWO MEN, TWO MACES.` → `A TEACHER ARRIVES.` → `BOTH ARE HIS STUDENTS.`

segments.voice: Balarama greets everyone, and he asks for the fight to move. In Ganguli's telling, they all walk to Samantapanchaka, ground held holy, so that a warrior who dies there dies in a sacred place. Then the two cousins close in. The epic gives the fight like weather: maces crashing, sparks flying, the two circling each other like bulls. Neither gives way. At the edge of the ground, Arjuna asks Krishna, in effect, which of them is better. Krishna's answer is careful. Bhima is the stronger. Duryodhana has put in more practice and has more skill. Fought by the rules, Bhima may not win. Then Krishna reminds Arjuna of something said years before, in the dice hall. When Draupadi was dragged in and insulted, Duryodhana bared his thigh to her, and Bhima vowed to break that thigh with his mace. Arjuna understands. Standing where Bhima can see him, he strikes his own thigh with his hand. Bhima sees it. When Duryodhana next leaps into the air, Bhima swings low, a blow the rules of mace fighting forbid, and breaks both his thighs. The king falls. This week ran from Karna's stuck wheel, through Shalya's command, to this one blow on a holy plain. And the teacher of both fighters has seen all of it.
screen: `MOVE TO HOLY GROUND` · `STRONGER VERSUS SKILLED` · `ARJUNA STRIKES HIS OWN THIGH` · then, large: `THE BLOW BELOW THE WAIST`

segments.voice: Rest your hands on your thighs and feel the strength in your legs that carries you all day without being asked. Then bring to mind a time someone signaled you without a word, a look or a gesture you understood at once. Hold that moment for a few breaths and see it clearly, or hold it in prayer if you pray.
Shalya. The book of the war's last day: a king out of the lake, a teacher arriving, and a vow kept with one blow below the waist.
Your line: a hand on his own thigh. Tomorrow, the teacher's anger. Day eight hundred forty-seven, done.

howItsDone: The mace fight between Bhima and Duryodhana is a favorite scene in retellings, dance-dramas and recitations of the Mahabharata, and Bhima is often shown in art holding his mace.

chat.says: How did Bhima win the mace fight if Duryodhana had more skill?
options: On Arjuna's signal, Bhima struck a forbidden blow and broke Duryodhana's thighs.
Balarama stepped in and showed Bhima where Duryodhana's guard was weak.
Duryodhana was still worn out from hiding, and slipped on the wet ground.
chat.meaning: Fought by the rules, Krishna said, Bhima might lose. Arjuna struck his own thigh, and Bhima kept his dice-hall vow with a forbidden blow.
